A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Random Feature Representation Boosting by the same authors. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across notation changes and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original OpenML regression and classification experiments and a synthetic point-cloud experiment, with measured performance and training times in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds feature-initialization ablations and larger-dataset experiments, including performance, timing, and uncertainty results.

M1.justification: The residual architecture, exact-greedy and gradient-greedy procedures, objectives, gradient fitting, and line search remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2. Renaming the learned map from Delta to A and evaluating Gaussian features within the already supported arbitrary-feature framework do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: V2 adds CoverType classification and YearPredictionMSD regression in Appendix E.5 while retaining the 91 OpenML datasets and concentric-circle task. Larger-sample experiments on OpenML IDs 23517 and 44975 revisit existing datasets; their increased sample counts are protocol changes rather than additional coverage.

E2.justification: The main OpenML and point-cloud comparator sets are retained. Appendix E.4 adds evaluated i.i.d.-Gaussian RFNN and RFRBoost variants alongside their SWIM counterparts in Tables 9–10. The larger-dataset experiments reuse existing baseline families.

E3.justification: Table 4 changes the E2E learning-rate search from 10^-7–10^-2 to 10^-6–10^-1 and XGBoost depth from 3–10 to 1–10. Point-cloud settings also change, including RFRBoost's boosting rate from 0.1 to 1.0 and E2E batch size from 64 to 128. New experiments introduce Gaussian-scale tuning and GPU learning curves using hold-out tests and 20% validation splits, alongside the retained nested five-fold benchmark protocol.

E4.justification: V1 already compares scalar, diagonal, and dense mappings and examines point-cloud representations. V2 adds an initialization ablation across regression and classification in Appendix E.4 and training-size sensitivity analyses of predictive performance and runtime in Appendix E.5. These address previously untested dependence on feature initialization and data scale.

E5.justification: Figures 2–3 change the significance threshold from 0.10 to 0.05 while retaining Wilcoxon testing with Holm correction. New scaling experiments report five different random seeds and 95% confidence bands in Figures 9–10. The point-cloud experiment retains its ten-run mean and standard-deviation reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 revise scores and timings: E2E regression RMSE changes from 0.4167 to 0.412, and point-cloud accuracy from 0.519 to 0.732, alongside changed settings; RFRBoost's point-cloud accuracy remains 0.997. V2 also adds dataset-level OpenML scores, initialization results, and scaling curves. Figure 10 shows E2E outperforming RFRBoost on three of four datasets at the largest tested sizes.

T1.justification: V2 adds a formal serial time-complexity expression in Section 3.5 and corrects the empirical-measure normalization in Section 2 by including 1/n. The principal closed-form solutions, excess-risk bound, and proofs in Appendices A–D are retained, largely with notation changes.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion now explicitly restrict superiority over RFNNs and E2E ResNets to the small- to medium-scale regime, whereas v1 states this without that explicit qualification. The central methodological, analytical-solution, and theoretical-guarantee contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix E.5 introduce substantive large-data limitations and motivate RFRBoost initialization followed by E2E fine-tuning as future work. Appendix E.4 adds an interpretation of modest initialization benefits versus training cost. However, its claim of 32 classification wins for i.i.d. features conflicts with Table 10 and Figure 7, which assign those wins to SWIM RFRBoost.

D1.justification: V2 supplies dataset identifiers with individual results, detailed larger-dataset splits and hyperparameter grids, Gaussian-scale settings, and NVIDIA RTX 6000 hardware information. It newly specifies the point-cloud allocation of 5,000 training/validation and 5,000 test points, classification solver, PyTorch implementation, and official XGBoost implementation. The code-access location is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds scattering-network literature, statistical-comparison references, and citations for software and the new datasets. It also identifies sandwiched least squares as a special case of generalized Sylvester equations. The broader positioning relative to boosting and random-feature research remains intact.

P1.justification: The existing narrative and section sequence are largely retained. V2 makes local prose corrections, renames mathematical symbols, adds short time-complexity and larger-dataset sections, extends Appendix E, and includes an impact statement. Author affiliations and publication information are reformatted.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the presentation with dataset-level tables, distribution plots, initialization-comparison displays, and scaling curves with confidence bands in Tables 5–7 and 9–11 and Figures 5–10. Existing main results are regrouped and Figure 4 is redrawn. V1's point-cloud settings table is retained as v2 Table 8.

improvement.justification: V1's tabular evaluation was capped at 5,000 observations and did not isolate initialization dependence or expose individual dataset results. V2 substantially strengthens empirical scrutiny through initialization ablations, seeded scaling experiments, detailed results, and reproducibility information. The larger-data findings reveal important limits and appropriately narrow the abstract and conclusion. The erroneous classification-win summary weakens reporting accuracy, but the overall gains in validation and claim calibration are substantial.
